The point of debate isn't to win. The point of debate understand why your opponent believes as they do and through rigorous wrestling understand why you believe what you do even more.
I believe every post isn't a debate.

The point of a debate is to sharpen and test your thesis to other opinions/information/critics so you can confirm or adjust your reasoning based on this new information. When debating correctly your viewpoint could even turn into something else or the opposite of your original opinion due to new information, when presented with other more sound/logical viewpoints. This is a very healthy way of reaching an educated opinion.

Unfortunatly the current popular debating style coming over from the USA is shouting your opinion as loud as you can to get your "right". When confronted with other viewpoints; Start throwing assumptions and discrediting your opponent to desperatly hold to your own opinion. These are not debates.......
that the smartest thing that has ever been said on vaot

Actually, I think it's pretty obvious the point of debate is to "win," just not in the simplistic sense of winning a game, but in the sense that you persuade the other party to your point of view along with (hopefully a majority) of whoever is paying attention. One key way to accomplish this is by understanding how and why your opponent thinks the way or what they do. If this process is done correctly, everyone comes out understanding why they believe what they do even more. The term "win" may not be the most appropriate, but there is absolutely a notion of success and failure when it comes to debate, formal or otherwise.

When I debate, I debate to 'lose'. I never back down but I hope that the other person brings up good points. Here are the possible outcomes for me:

1) He 'wins' so I learn something new. 2) Tie, my ideas grow stronger, I understand them better 3) I win after a long contest, my ideas are stronger and I have gained an ally.

In any of these scenarios, I gain value from the outcomes. I never lose because I always gain something. That is what I get from having an open mind and listening to my opponent.

In reality options 1 and 3 so rarely happen that it is almost not worth counting them, but they do happen on occasion.

First, I want to acknowledge that I understand what you're saying, which is that one should not approach discussion with an adversarial attitude. In regular discourse, when the participants have a humble attitude such as the one you describe everyone wins. However, debate is a specific type of discourse where the explicit purpose is to persuade. If you approach a debate to lose, as you put it, you will fail at debating.

The crux here is that the term debate has a specific meaning. If we start conflating terms that are similar, yet distinctly different, we break language and speech as a form of communication. Don't do this.
You're right. I guess debate is used to liberally. People really don't do that anymore.
I'll tell you what though, you obviously have the right mentality in the sense that it seems your primary goal is to learn rather than just being or feeling right. Keep at it.
I think we were meaning 'win' in different senses. Usually 'win' just means last man standing which is why scream at eachother debating has taken over. Everyone loses in that form of debate.

No, this is a dangerously over simplified notion of winning. Win is a very contextualized word. For example, winning an informal debate is not same as winning a soccer game. Obviously, in team sports there is no debate or discussion, and if one team decides to stand around and shout at their opponents, the other can simply score more goals.
